summary: PAEMS is a qubit-error model with $O(n^2)$ complexity that captures spatial heterogeneity, temporal error accumulation, and leakage propagation in superconducting QPUs by using qubit-specific depolarizing channels initialized from calibration and optimized via CMA-ES on repetition-code datasets. On IBM Brisbane, Sherbrooke, and Torino, PAEMS achieves 19.5×, 9.3×, and 5.2× reductions in timelike, spacelike, and spacetime error-correlation differences versus prior models, and shows 58–73% lower total variation distance than Google's SI1000 across five QPU platforms.
motivation: QEC decoder training requires massive synthetic error datasets, but superconducting QPUs cannot generate them directly due to scale and cost constraints; existing models based on uniform, Markovian, or phenomenological assumptions fail to capture realistic correlated detection-event statistics and spatiotemporal error dynamics.
method: PAEMS employs a circuit-level framework with asymmetric depolarizing channels for decoherence (parameterized by calibrated $T_1$, $T_2$, operation duration), symmetric depolarizing channels for gate errors, distinct SPAM error probabilities per qubit for initialization and reset, and explicit leakage/seepage processes; parameters are initialized from platform calibration and optimized using CMA-ES on multi-round repetition-code measurements from target QPUs.
result: On 30-round repetition codes with 21 qubits on Torino, PAEMS reproduces timelike correlations (e.g., 0.337 ± 0.008 vs. measured 0.335 ± 0.012 for ancilla qubit 1) with 19.5× correlation-difference improvement over SI1000, and captures leakage-induced error accumulation with root-mean-square detection-event-fraction error of $3.4 	imes 10^{-3}$; single-round experiments across Brisbane, Wuyue, and Tianyan show TVD reductions of 69.4%, 58.1%, and 68.9% respectively versus SI1000.
